classification.difficultyReason: Apply the definitions of intersection and union directly to shade the overlap or both circles.

spec.description: An unshaded universal-set rectangle containing two overlapping circles, A on the left and B on the right.
spec.mathematics: The student shades the intersection of A and B.

answer.short: Shade only the overlap of $A$ and $B$.
answer.worked: $A\cap B$ contains the elements in both sets. Shade only their overlapping region.

spec.description: Only the overlapping lens is shaded light blue.
spec.mathematics: The shaded region is A intersection B.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer shading appears only in the solution.

spec.description: An unshaded universal-set rectangle containing two overlapping circles, A on the left and B on the right.
spec.mathematics: The student shades the union of A and B.

answer.short: Shade both circles, including the overlap.
answer.worked: $A\cup B$ contains the elements in $A$ or $B$, including those in both. Shade all of both circles.

spec.description: Both circles, including their overlap, are shaded light blue; the outside region remains unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The shaded region is A union B.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer shading appears only in the solution.
